definitions.explanation: A girl or woman who has been legally adopted into a family. The female counterpart of {養子|ようし} (adopted child, traditionally male).

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{養女|ようじょ}として{迎|むか}えられた。
examples.english: She was taken in as an adopted daughter.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもがいなかった{夫婦|ふうふ}は、{養女|ようじょ}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: The childless couple adopted a daughter.

examples.japanese: {歴史的|れきしてき}に、{家業|かぎょう}を{継|つ}がせるために{養女|ようじょ}を{取|と}り、その{夫|おっと}を{婿養子|むこようし}として{迎|むか}えることがあった。
examples.english: Historically, families would sometimes adopt a daughter and bring in her husband as an adopted son-in-law to continue the family business.

notes:
The formal term for an adopted daughter, as opposed to {養子|ようし} which can mean adopted child in general but traditionally refers to an adopted son.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {養女|ようじょ}を{迎|むか}える: to adopt a daughter
- {養女|ようじょ}として{育|そだ}てる: to raise as an adopted daughter
- {養女|ようじょ}に{出|だ}す: to give up (a daughter) for adoption

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japan, adoption was often strategic — to secure an heir for a family line. Adopting a daughter ({養女|ようじょ}) and then bringing in a son-in-law ({婿養子|むこようし}) was one way to continue a family name.

RELATED WORDS:
- {養子|ようし}: adopted child (general/male)
- {養母|ようぼ}: adoptive mother
- {養父|ようふ}: adoptive father
- {養親|ようしん}: adoptive parent
- {実子|じっし}: biological child
